title: Championship Round 2: Prophetic Literature & Planetary Cosmologies
description: 50 high-difficulty competition questions: 25 advanced theological & biblical inquiries plus 25 elite general knowledge challenges.

questions.question_text: In the Book of Daniel, which angel explains the vision of the ram and the goat in chapter 8?
questions.explanation: Daniel 8:16 records a human voice calling: 'Gabriel, make this man understand the vision.'

questions.question_text: Who was the priest of Midian whose daughter Zipporah became the wife of Moses?
questions.explanation: Exodus 2:16-21 and 3:1 identify Jethro (also known as Reuel), priest of Midian, as Moses's father-in-law.

questions.question_text: In the Gospel of John, by what pool with five roofed colonnades did Jesus heal a man invalided for 38 years?
questions.explanation: John 5:2 states: 'Now there is in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate a pool, in Aramaic called Bethesda, which has five roofed colonnades.'

questions.question_text: Which king of Israel was famously rebuked by the prophet Elijah for seizing Naboth's vineyard?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:17-19 records the word of the Lord coming to Elijah to confront King Ahab in the vineyard of Naboth.

questions.question_text: According to Acts 18, what was the trade shared by Paul, Aquila, and Priscilla in Corinth?
questions.explanation: Acts 18:3 notes that Paul stayed and worked with Aquila and Priscilla because they were tentmakers by trade.

questions.question_text: Which Old Testament queen traveled from southern Arabia with camels bearing spices and gold to test Solomon with hard questions?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 10:1-2 chronicles the Queen of Sheba arriving in Jerusalem to test King Solomon with riddles and hard questions.

questions.question_text: What was the name of the runaway slave on whose behalf Paul penned a personal letter to Philemon?
questions.explanation: In Philemon 1:10, Paul appeals for his spiritual child Onesimus, whose name means 'useful'.

questions.question_text: Which prophet was thrown into a muddy cistern belonging to Malchiah during the siege of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 38:6 recounts Jeremiah being cast into the dungeon of Malchiah, sinking into the mire until rescued by Ebed-melech.

questions.question_text: In Genesis 14, to whom did Abram pay a tenth of all the spoils after rescuing Lot?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:18-20 records Melchizedek king of Salem bringing out bread and wine, and Abram giving him a tenth of everything.

questions.question_text: Which Roman officer was stationed in Caesarea and described as the first Gentile convert following Peter's vision?
questions.explanation: Acts 10:1-2 introduces Cornelius, a centurion of the Italian Cohort, a devout and God-fearing man.

questions.question_text: What type of tree did the tax collector Zacchaeus climb in Jericho in order to see Jesus?
questions.explanation: Luke 19:4 tells how Zacchaeus ran ahead and climbed a sycamore-fig tree because he was short in stature.

questions.question_text: In Judges 4, which woman slew the Canaanite general Sisera with a tent peg and hammer while he slept?
questions.explanation: Judges 4:21 details Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, taking a tent peg and hammer and driving it through Sisera's temple.

questions.question_text: What town was the birthplace of both King David and Jesus Christ?
questions.explanation: Micah 5:2 and Luke 2:4 identify Bethlehem Ephrathah as the ancestral city of David and the birthplace of the Messiah.

questions.question_text: Who was struck down dead at Perez-uzzah after reaching out his hand to steady the Ark of God?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 6:6-7 records Uzzah putting forth his hand to the ark when the oxen stumbled, and the anger of the Lord burning against him.

questions.question_text: Which prophet saw a valley full of dry bones that rattled together and became filled with breath?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:1-10 details Ezekiel's famous vision of the valley of dry bones revived into a vast army.

questions.question_text: On which island was the Apostle John exiled when he received the visions recorded in Revelation?
questions.explanation: Revelation 1:9 states: 'I, John... was on the island called Patmos on account of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.'

questions.question_text: Which judge of Israel made a rash vow before battle against the Ammonites that affected his only daughter?
questions.explanation: Judges 11:30-35 recounts Jephthah's solemn vow to sacrifice whatever first came out of his house to meet him.

questions.question_text: What was the name of the sorcerer on Cyprus who was struck blind by Paul in Acts 13?
questions.explanation: Acts 13:6-11 records Paul rebuking the magician Elymas (Bar-Jesus), causing a mist and darkness to fall upon him.

questions.question_text: Which king of Israel instituted the worship of two golden calves at Bethel and Dan to prevent pilgrims from going to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:28-29 recounts Jeroboam making two golden calves and setting one in Bethel and the other in Dan.

questions.question_text: Who was the female merchant of purple cloth from Thyatira whose heart was opened by God in Philippi?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:14 records Lydia of Thyatira listening to Paul and being baptized alongside her entire household.

questions.question_text: Which Psalm begins with the famous words: 'The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?'
questions.explanation: Psalm 27:1 opens with: 'The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The Lord is the stronghold of my life.'

questions.question_text: In Matthew 27, what was the field bought with the thirty silver coins returned by Judas called?
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:7-8 and Acts 1:19 identify the potter's field as Akeldama, that is, the Field of Blood.

questions.question_text: Which prophet confronted King David with the parable of the rich man who took the poor man's single ewe lamb?
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:1-7 details the prophet Nathan telling David the parable and concluding with 'You are the man!'

questions.question_text: In 2 Kings 2, how was the prophet Elijah taken up into heaven?

options.B: In a whirlwind with chariots of fire
options.C: On the wings of an eagle

questions.explanation: 2 Kings 2:11 states: 'Behold, chariots of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them. And Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.'

questions.question_text: What is the Hebrew name of the Feast of Booths (Tabernacles) celebrated in the seventh month?
questions.explanation: Leviticus 23:34 establishes the Feast of Booths (Sukkot), beginning on the 15th day of the seventh month Tishrei.

questions.question_text: What is the only planet in the Solar System whose axial tilt exceeds 90 degrees, causing it to rotate nearly on its side?
questions.explanation: Uranus has an extreme axial tilt of approximately 97.8 degrees, meaning its rotational axis points almost directly at the Sun.

questions.question_text: Which treaty ended the War of the Spanish Succession in 1713, reshaping balance-of-power diplomacy in Europe?
questions.explanation: The Peace of Utrecht (1713) ended the War of the Spanish Succession, confirming Philip V as king while prohibiting uniting French and Spanish crowns.

questions.question_text: What fundamental particle is the mediator or gauge boson of the electromagnetic force in the Standard Model?
questions.explanation: In quantum electrodynamics, the massless photon is the gauge boson responsible for carrying the electromagnetic interaction.

questions.question_text: Which sea is considered the saltiest open-water marginal sea in the world due to extreme evaporation and lack of river discharge?
questions.explanation: The Red Sea reaches surface salinities of 40 to 41 practical salinity units (PSU), the highest among open marginal marine bodies.

questions.question_text: Who synthesized the first synthetic organic dye, mauveine (aniline purple), in 1856 while attempting to produce quinine?
questions.explanation: At age 18, English chemist William Henry Perkin accidentally discovered mauveine, founding the synthetic dye and petrochemical industry.

questions.question_text: In vertebrate anatomy, what is the largest and longest nerve in the human body?
questions.explanation: The sciatic nerve arises from spinal nerves L4 through S3 and extends down through the pelvis into each lower limb.

questions.question_text: Which ancient philosopher formulated the Allegory of the Cave in Book VII of 'The Republic'?
questions.explanation: Plato presented the Allegory of the Cave to explore the nature of philosophical enlightenment and the world of Forms versus sensory shadows.

questions.question_text: What is the only element on the periodic table that sublimes under standard atmospheric pressure rather than melting into a liquid?
questions.explanation: At standard atmospheric pressure (1 atm), carbon has no liquid phase and sublimes directly to gas at approximately 3915 K (3642 °C).

questions.question_text: Which African nation was never colonized during the Scramble for Africa, famously defeating the Italian invasion at Adwa in 1896?
questions.explanation: Under Emperor Menelik II, the Ethiopian Empire decisively crushed the invading Italian army at the Battle of Adwa on March 1, 1896.

questions.question_text: What mathematical constant is defined as the limit of (1 + 1/n)^n as n approaches infinity, approximately 2.71828?
questions.explanation: The mathematical constant e, discovered by Jacob Bernoulli in connection with compound interest, is the base of the natural logarithm.

questions.question_text: What architectural style characterized by pointed arches, ribbed vaults, and flying buttresses flourished in medieval Europe from the 12th century?
questions.explanation: Gothic architecture originated in 12th-century France (Abbey Church of Saint-Denis) enabling monumental height and stained-glass lighting.

questions.question_text: Which Danish astronomer lost part of his nose in a duel and compiled planetary observation data without a telescope that Kepler later used?
questions.explanation: Tycho Brahe built Uraniborg and meticulously recorded planetary motions, which allowed his assistant Johannes Kepler to derive the laws of planetary motion.

questions.question_text: What enzyme found in tears, saliva, and human mucus hydrolyzes peptidoglycan in bacterial cell walls?
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered lysozyme in 1921; it acts as an innate immune defense by breaking beta-(1,4)-glycosidic bonds in bacterial walls.

questions.question_text: Which South American lake, situated between Bolivia and Peru at 3,812 meters elevation, is the highest navigable commercial lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Titicaca in the high Andes plateau is by volume of water and surface area the largest lake in South America and the highest navigable body.

questions.question_text: What type of chemical bond involves the equal sharing of electron pairs between two atoms of identical electronegativity?
questions.explanation: In nonpolar covalent bonds (such as in diatomic H2 or O2), bonding electrons are shared symmetrically with no net dipole moment.

questions.question_text: Who was the primary architect of the Palace of Versailles expansion under King Louis XIV?

options.A: Louis Le Vau and Jules Hardouin-Mansart

questions.explanation: Louis Le Vau designed the initial monumental envelope, and Jules Hardouin-Mansart later designed the Hall of Mirrors and grand wings of Versailles.

questions.question_text: Which constitutional amendment abolished slavery throughout the entire United States in December 1865?
questions.explanation: The Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution officially prohibited slavery and involuntary servitude except as punishment for a crime.

questions.question_text: What is the study of inscriptions and ancient epigraphs engraved on stone, metal, or durable materials called?
questions.explanation: Epigraphy is the primary historical science concerned with deciphering, classifying, and interpreting inscriptions carved on enduring media.

questions.question_text: In statistical mechanics, whose constant (k_B) relates the average kinetic energy of particles in a gas with its thermodynamic temperature?
questions.explanation: Ludwig Boltzmann formulated the connection between macroscopic entropy and microstates: S = k_B * ln(W).

questions.question_text: Which island archipelago located off the tip of South America is divided between Chile and Argentina?
questions.explanation: Tierra del Fuego ('Land of Fire') is an archipelago separated from the South American mainland by the Strait of Magellan.

questions.question_text: What is the primary protein component of human hair, fingernails, and the outer stratum corneum of skin?
questions.explanation: Alpha-keratin is a fibrous structural protein rich in cysteine amino acids whose disulfide bridges confer high mechanical stability.

questions.question_text: Which Russian chemist arranged the known chemical elements in order of increasing atomic mass in 1869, predicting undiscovered elements?
questions.explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev formulated the Periodic Law and correctly predicted the properties of then-unknown elements like gallium and germanium.

questions.question_text: What is the capital city of New Zealand, known as the southernmost sovereign capital city in the world?
questions.explanation: Wellington, situated on the southwestern tip of the North Island along Cook Strait, has been New Zealand's capital since 1865.

questions.question_text: Who directed the 1968 landmark epic science fiction film '2001: A Space Odyssey'?
questions.explanation: Stanley Kubrick produced and directed '2001: A Space Odyssey', co-writing the screenplay with science fiction author Arthur C. Clarke.

questions.question_text: What physical quantity does the area underneath a velocity-versus-time graph represent in one-dimensional kinematics?
questions.explanation: Because velocity is the time derivative of position (v = dx/dt), the definite integral of velocity with respect to time yields the displacement.
